PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called the meeting to order at 5:09 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:10 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:18 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: City Council has not finished discussion on item and will be reconvening to Closed Session upon completion of the regular City Council meeting.  

Items #1 and #2  - Staff made a presentation, the City Council provided direction to staff and no reportable action was taken on these items.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular meeting to order at 6:19 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Acting Public Works Director Nila led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. 64th City Birthday Celebration & Cake Cutting Ceremony Director Alaniz and Mayor Argumedo started the 64th City Birthday celebration with opening remarks. The Unplugged Team then performed the Happy Birthday song and a cake was cut ceremonially.  Mayor Argumedo called the break at 6:18 p.m. The City COuncil returned from the break at 6:49 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT Nick Padilla thanked the City Council for the opportunities that Commerce kids had received, and expressed pride in his daughter's honor roll achievement.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Mayor stated that the City staff requested item #4 to be continued to the next City Council meeting, and Councilmember Lainez asked to pull item #5 from the agenda for discussion.  

Item #5 - Councilmember Lainez commended staff for securing nearly $1.3 million in funding through a program that allows the city to receive funding for operational and maintenance activities related to Well 4. This is a significant benefit for the city, as it helps to recoup water system expenses. 

Councilmember Lainez moved, seconded by Councilmember Rebollo, to adopt a Resolution approving a Memorandum of Understanding by and between City of Commerce and the Water Replenishment District of Southern California regarding technical for Proposition 68 Groundwater – Drinking Water Treatment Operations and Maintenance Funding Program.  The motion carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamriano and Mayor Argumedo (5)


4.. Fifth Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Stantec Architecture, Incorporated

5.. Drinking Water Treatment Operations and Maintenance Funding Program

3.. Approval of Minutes

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 11A, and 11B

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.. Committee and Commission Appointments Vice Mayor Altamirano appointed Beatriz Del Rosario De Jimenez to the Senior Citizens Commission.

6.. Eastern Avenue Transit Hub  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Acting Public Works Director Nila introduced Scott Ma from Hartzog & Grabill Inc., who delivered a presentation advocating for the approval of Option #3.

Discussions ensued regarding collision statistics and the appropriateness of C lane for the street. Mr. Ma suggested that if buses were not in the hub, bicyclists could use it instead of entering the vehicle lane. Councilmember Lainez proposed incorporating green paint on bike lane for enhanced safety, while Vice Mayor Altamirano favored Option 2 and acquiring an easement for the bus hub. Acting Director Nila mentioned the owner's disinterest in granting the easement.

Councilmember Garcia suggested relocating the bus hub within the city, prompting Acting Director Nila to highlight the need for another study and funding from Measure AA. Director of Transportation McFerguson emphasized the cost-effectiveness of Option 2 over moving the bus hub. Councilmember Garcia raised concerns about recent Metro bus routes turning right on Harbor street, and discussions continued regarding the possibility of maintaining through traffic on Jillson Street without restricting it to right turns only. Councilmember Garcia proposed leaving that intersection as is and possibly installing flashing lights, a recommendation endorsed by the Mayor.




7.. Speed & Reckless Driving Exhibition Ordinance Review  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Public Safety Manager Epson presented an overview of the staff report. In response to Vice Mayor Altamirano's inquiry about the implementation of administrative fines in the City, Epson stated that administrative fines issued but clarified that the judge retained the authority to adjust or dismiss the fines.

During the discussion on fines for spectators and the administrative process, Public Safety Manager Epson explained that administrative fines are processed through the City Attorney but still undergo judicial review. Mayor Argumedo proposed incorporating a provision in the ordinance mandating that violators undergo the Street Racing Kills program.

Public Safety Manager Epson stated that deputies could issue administrative fines. Councilmember Rebollo advocated for increased enforcement and citations. Sergeant Duarte acknowledged the challenges of addressing swiftly evolving street racing events but highlighted efforts to identify vehicles later for citation and towing.


PUBLIC HEARING

9.. Resolution Adopting Certain Fundings and Approving Energy Services Contract for Energy Related Improvements to City Facilities with Alliance Building Solutions, Inc. and Associated Financing with Alliance Funding Solutions, Inc, in the Form of a Tax-Exempt Lease - Continuance of this Item to the Next City Council Meeting  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano

ORDINANCES

10.. Adoption and Second Reading of Ordinance to Repeal Ordinance No. 784, to Revoke Development Agreement No. 784 Related to a Commercial Cannabis Permit Application No. 18-069  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway provided a brief overview.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia mentioned that she had discussions with the new Public Safety Manager Epson and requested a thorough review and update of existing policies, performance evaluations, and corrective actions as needed. Additionally, Councilmember Garcia emphasized the importance of creating an emergency response handbook specifically for elected officials and staff, and have an emergency department up and running.

Councilmember Rebollo shared her participation in various events, including a COG meeting, Metro West Side Branch Line engagement, and a meeting with the president of East Los Angeles College. She expressed enthusiasm about potential partnerships and exciting developments for the city.

Mayor Argumedo informed the council about his attendance at the Southeast Gold Line extension event. He highlighted the upcoming stop behind Citadel, emphasizing its potential to address traffic issues previously faced by the city.

The Councilmembers and the Mayor extended their collective wishes to the city for its 64th birthday.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 8:37 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.
